The protected-file human-copy governance boundary is testable: AC-017 (requirements.md :789) requires a pre-edit grep re-check of `guard-invariants.json` before any direct edit; AC-031 (requirements.md :803) requires a three-way exact-set/hash/post-copy-verification match for the human-copy runner; Roles and Permissions (requirements.md :923-967) fixes that only a human/spec-review-loop may flip `Spec-Review-Status`/`Impl-Review-Status` to `Passed`; AC-025 (requirements.md :797) makes `check-workflow-state.sh` exit 0 (which enforces the Pending/Passed field state) a testable registration-time condition. These boundaries are structurally testable independent of the ASSUMPTIONS-RESOLVABLE/DOWNSTREAM-READINESS gap noted above (that gap is about content-completeness of one payload target, not about whether the approval/governance mechanism itself is testable).

Same evidence as ASSUMPTIONS-RESOLVABLE, applied to the handoff-readiness failure mode: AC-010 (requirements.md :782) and AC-031 (requirements.md :803) commit this package to staging `.github/workflows/test.yml` as a protected-file payload target with exact-hash verification, but no REQ text (REQ-001 through REQ-006, requirements.md :229-666) states what functional change that file requires, or why a CI workflow edit is within this feature's scope at all -- `investigation.md` never discusses it (zero grep matches). A design.md author (or the design reviewer evaluating design.md) would have to invent the actual product behavior/content of that CI change, which is exactly the missing-product-behavior-invention failure mode DOWNSTREAM-READINESS exists to catch. Every other REQ in this package cites a specific investigation.md finding or sibling-epic text grounding its scope; this one payload target is the sole exception.
